doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Extended family in St. Louis and childhood nicknames
summary: Asked about family, he describes the St. Louis relatives, Aunt Nannie's biscuits, and nicknames such as Long George Kelly and George Allen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I asked you who gave you your drum kit, because I was just interested in, what was the family structure for you? Did you have any brothers or sisters or cousins who were around a lot?

I can’t say that. No. My mother had friends that we used to visit every – in St. Louis – visit every year. They were musical too, and St. Louis was a musical city. But in those days, everybody was your aunt.
Any kind of an extended family.
So my Aunt Nannie in St. Louis, what she was good at was cooking biscuits.
Well that’s important, though. What did they call you, George?
Because we have the formal names, but the childhood names are always interesting.
One of my names was Kelly, because we played basketball and we played baseball, and I’d throw the baseball out of the park. So they called me Long George Kelly.
Long George Kelly. Now that name came from the kids, some of the kids?
What about your mom? Did she have a name for you, a little special name, a little affectionate name?
George Allen. That was the name. Never George. Just George Allen.
George Allen, okay. And any of the other extended family have any names for you, other than your given name?
George Allen. “George Allen, come in the house.”
